subskill: No-solution parameter splits an inside-band count
prompt:
kx + 30 = 12x + 10k
In the equation above, k is a constant. Of the integers k from -20 to 40, inclusive, how many make the equation have a solution x with 4 ≤ x ≤ 19?
explanation: Collect the x terms: kx - 12x = 10k - 30, so (k - 12)x = 10k - 30. When k = 12 this reads 0 = 90, so the equation has no solution and k = 12 never counts. For every other k, x = (10k - 30)/(k - 12) = 10 + 90/(k - 12). If k > 12, then x is greater than 10, so x ≥ 4 automatically, and x ≤ 19 exactly when 90/(k - 12) ≤ 9, that is, k - 12 ≥ 10, so k ≥ 22: the integers 22 through 40, which is 19 values. If k < 12, then x is less than 10, so x ≤ 19 automatically, and x ≥ 4 exactly when 90/(12 - k) ≤ 6, that is, 12 - k ≥ 15, so k ≤ -3: the integers -20 through -3, which is 18 values. The count is 19 + 18 = 37. Choice 26 comes from finding that x = 4 when k = -3 and x = 19 when k = 22 and then counting the integers from -3 to 22, as if x moved steadily from 4 to 19 as k goes from -3 to 22; but k = 12, where there is no solution, lies in between, and every k strictly between -3 and 22 actually gives an x outside the band. Choice 19 comes from multiplying 4 ≤ (10k - 30)/(k - 12) ≤ 19 through by k - 12 without reversing the inequalities when k - 12 is negative, which keeps only k ≥ 22. Choice 16 counts the integers x from 4 to 19 instead of the values of k.
solve: let n = 0; for (let k = -20; k <= 40; k++) { if (k === 12) continue; const x = (10 * k - 30) / (k - 12); if (x >= 4 && x <= 19) n++; } return String(n);

distractor_solve.26: const kAt4 = 12 - 90 / (10 - 4); const kAt19 = 12 + 90 / (19 - 10); let n = 0; for (let k = -20; k <= 40; k++) { if (k >= kAt4 && k <= kAt19) n++; } return String(n);
distractor_solve.16: let n = 0; for (let x = 4; x <= 19; x++) n++; return String(n);

mechanism: inside-band count on both sides of the no-solution value
quantity_asked: the number of integers k from -20 to 40 for which the equation has a solution between 4 and 19 inclusive

setup.i: k is in the x-coefficient on one side and in the constant on the other side of a one-variable equation, so the solution is 10 + 90/(k - 12) and k = 12 gives no solution
setup.ii: the solution lies in a closed band that contains the value the solution approaches (10), so qualifying k lie on both sides of the no-solution value, far from it
setup.iii: number of integer values of k in a stated range

plugback.why: The key is at natural try 4 (largest option). A student trying 16, 19 and 26 first cannot test them by substitution - each is a count of k values, not a k or an x - so every check needs the full two-branch analysis; there is no one-step confirmation at any try.
plugback.aggregate_over: the integers k from -20 to 40, other than the no-solution value k = 12, whose solution lies between 4 and 19 inclusive

26.why: Counting the integers between the two boundary k values assumes the solution moves steadily as k goes from -3 to 22, skipping the no-solution value k = 12 inside; whether that count is above or below the truth depends on how far the stated range reaches beyond -3 and 22, which the stem does not signal.

19.why: Multiplying by k - 4 without reversing for negative k - 4 keeps only one branch; nothing in the stem reveals which branch survives or how large it is.

16.why: Counting x values in the band instead of k values gives a number fixed by the band, unrelated in size to the k-range; the stem does not say whether that is more or fewer than the qualifying k.

counter_error.solve: let n = 0; for (let k = -20; k <= 40; k++) { if (k !== 12) n++; } return String(n);
counter_error.why: A student who checks only that the equation has a solution (k not 12) and forgets the band counts every k but 12, landing at 60, above the key and not an option.

far_distractor.why: The between-the-boundaries count ordinarily overshoots, because it sweeps in the k values right next to the no-solution value; here the qualifying k are the far ones on both sides and the stated range is long, so the same error lands below the key.

structure_check: The answer is the union of two rays cut off by the stated range, not an extremum or a universal condition, so no structural fact says that every slip lowers it: losing a branch lowers it, but forgetting the band (counter_error 60) raises it. The key being the largest option is not readable from the structure.
cheap_bound_check: The cheapest stem bound is that the count is at most 60 (61 integers in the range minus the no-solution value k = 12); every option, including the three distractors, sits on the key's side of it, so it strikes nothing.
intermediate_check: 26: no - it counts the k between the two boundary values, a complementary set; 37 does not follow from 26 through one printed relation. 19: no - it is one branch; reaching 37 needs the other branch's 18, which is not printed. 16: no - it is the number of integers in the printed band, and 37 does not follow from it by any printed relation.
shape_check: Properties handed over: the answer is a whole number, at least 0, at most 60. All four options (16, 19, 26, 37) survive every one together; no parity, sign or cap singles any out (two even, two odd).
interior_parity_check: The two middle values are 19 and 26: both two-digit whole numbers; the key 37 is not cleaner than them.
arith_class_check: The key 37 is not alone in a class the stem implies: 19 and 37 are odd, 16 and 26 even; 37 is not a multiple of a printed coefficient; it is not a printed number.
